purpose: Pegcetacoplan is used to treat certain blood and eye conditions. Empaveli treats a rare blood disorder called paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH), where the immune system mistakenly destroys red blood cells. Syfovre is used to slow down the progression of geographic atrophy, which is an advanced form of age-related macular degeneration that can lead to vision loss.
how_it_works: Your immune system has a defense system called the complement system, which normally helps fight infections. In some diseases, this system goes into overdrive and starts attacking your own cells or tissues. Pegcetacoplan works by blocking a key protein called C3, which stops this runaway immune response and helps protect your red blood cells or the cells in your eyes from being damaged.
common_side_effects: Injection site reactions such as pain, redness, or swelling where the shot is given; feeling tired or fatigued; infections; diarrhea; stomach pain; headache; and dizziness. Some people may also notice bruising at the injection site.
warnings: This medication carries a serious risk of bacterial infections, especially from germs like Neisseria meningitidis (meningococcal disease), which can be life-threatening. You must be vaccinated against meningococcal bacteria before starting this medicine. Tell your doctor right away if you develop fever, headache, stiff neck, or feel very sick, as these could be signs of a dangerous infection. You should also carry a medical alert card provided by your doctor while on this medication.
typical_dosing: For PNH (Empaveli): It is usually given as an injection under the skin twice a week, with a dose of 1080 mg each time. For geographic atrophy (Syfovre): It is given as an injection directly into the eye by your eye doctor, either once a month or once every other month, depending on your treatment plan.
